issue: 'Take my spear and do not cry out' is addressed to the brother (VOC bʰréh₂ter) but sléh₂gʷtu is IMP.3SG and mē HréwdHt a 3sg injunctive; 2sg sl̥h₂gʷdʰí/sléh₂gʷ and mē HréwdHs are needed. Minor: 'wounded' and 'beside him' not rendered.
'Sit down, wife, and eat' (VOC pótni) uses IMP.3SG sédtu, h₁ḗdtu ('let her sit, let her eat'); 2sg séd/sddʰí, h₁éddʰi needed. Minor: h₁ḗdtu with lengthened grade is an odd 3sg imperative.

(1) bʰréh₂terh₁e sédyetām píph₃et-kʷe: the coordinated 'drinking' is 3SG beside 3DU sédyetām with the same dual subject; píph₃etām needed. (2) 'Stand, and take your spear' uses IMP.3SG stnéh₂tu, h₁éptu. (3) 'Do not strike your brother!' (mother to son) uses 3sg mē stunédt. Minor: stnéh₂ti is 'place' rather than intransitive 'stand'.
Nominal 'h₁íd h₁wr̥Hú' + 'grew dark' renders 'It was broad and getting dark'; h₁íd neuter for móri; hortative 1pl; h₁íns for the men. Fine.
Wife to departing husband: 'Go', 'Remember me', 'Come back to me' are IMP.3SG linékʷtu, memóntu, gʷm̥yétu; 2sg forms needed. Optative wishes are fine.

Father to son (téwe, twé): 'Hear my words' ḱléwsetu IMP.3SG, 'do not lie / do not flee' mē dʰrugʰyét / mē bʰéwgt 3sg injunctives, 'Now go' h₁éytu IMP.3SG; all should be 2sg (ḱléwse, mē dʰrugʰyés, mē bʰéwgs, h₁idʰí). Minor: 'If you do this' rendered with relative h₁yód + ḱód.
'wild' horse not rendered (márkos alone); 'the hero led it away' has no overt subject after h₁éḱwos stéh₂t, so the PIE reads 'the horse stood up and led him' (subject continuity). Otherwise good.
Accusative of goal nókʷtm̥ h₁nédʰt / h₃réǵm̥ bʰoréyet accepted; the hero's speech has no verb of saying but is clear in context.

márkōs pró dréms: dréms is AOR.2SG with a plural subject 'the horses ran forward'; 3pl dr̥mént needed (sth₂éh₁yont next is 3pl). Minor: nos 'our' is the enclitic accusative/dative-genitive (Ved. naḥ), acceptable.
Tier 1 transcription: gʷah₂t with a-colouring, km̥tá unaccented convention clash, wérunos as a theonym; faithful to source.

'for many nights' polh₁úm (ACC.SG.m) does not agree with nékʷtsu (LOC.PL); acc. of duration polh₁úns nókʷtn̥s or loc polh₁úsu nékʷtsu expected. Present bʰérete in the relative for past 'carried'. Otherwise good: 2pl imperatives to the horses.
'Give me your horses and cattle' (téwe) uses IMP.3SG déh₃tu; dh₃dʰí/déh₃ needed. Minor: 'I will not give' is mē + 1sg subjunctive (prohibitive 'let me not') where ne is expected for a refusal.
h₁éḱwōs h₁ím h₂wisént pró-kʷe drémt: 'ran forward' is 3SG with the plural horses (the coordinated h₂wisént is 3pl); dr̥mént needed. Minor: double accusative yugóm for 'to the yoke'.
Dative address to Sky and Earth, then VOC déywōs + 2pl imperatives; optative wishes 'let him hear / say'. Fine (a dual to the pair would be finer).

'My fire!' in a string of vocatives (dʰwór, h₂éǵre) is ph₂wénh₁, the instrumental singular; vocative péh₂wr̥ needed. Minor: h₁ésyo 'his (another's)' for the man's own home where swóm is expected; mē + 1sg subjunctive for 'I shall not come back' (ne expected).

Brother to sister: 'Drink the water' péh₃tu, 'Remember your sister' memóntu, 'come back' h₁r̥sḱétu are IMP.3SG, while the coordinated 'take this gift' h₁áyso is correctly 2sg. Should be ph₃dʰí/péh₃, 2sg memonth₂é or IMP, h₁r̥sḱé.

(1) téwe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰiteh₂i h₁syéh₁t: the predicate adjective is LOC.SG.f; nom. sg. n. ń̥dʰgʷʰitom needed for neuter ḱléwos. (2) 'Gods, protect him' (VOC déywōs) uses IMP.3SG péh₂stu; 2pl ph₂sté needed.
'If I die, tell my mother' addressed to the comrade uses IMP.3SG sékʷtu; 2sg needed. Rest good: neuter plural gʷéruh₂ + 3sg péh₃eti, duals sédyetām / píph₃etām légʰyetām.

péh₂wr̥ h₁ím dʰéh₁t 'put fire into it': h₁ím is masculine but the antecedent dʰwórm̥ is feminine; h₁íh₂m̥ needed (84dc906d uses h₁íh₂m̥ for the door). Minor: h₁éterōs 'the other (of two)' for 'the others' of many; mē + 1sg subjunctive for 'I will not flee'.
Tier 1 Schleicher title in 1868 notation (awis akwāsas ka), wholly unlike corpus notation; faithful to source.
'Stand aside from the door' said to the strong one uses IMP.3SG léyttu; 2sg needed. Otherwise good: ḱā́m dʰwórm̥ and h₁íh₂m̥ feminine for the door, ablative dʰurés, bahuvrihi h₁suḱléwēs.
Tier 1 line: h₃rḗḱs with devoiced ḱ, root-accented súHnum against the lexicon's suHnúm, unaccented wl̥nh₁to; source conventions.

To the smith: 'Make me a spear' tḗtḱtu, and the smith's 'Take it' sléh₂gʷtu and 'Do not give me a gift' mē dédeh₃t are all 3sg (IMP / injunctive); 2sg needed. Minor: gʷéru 'spit' then ǵʰoysóm for the same spear; stunédt 'push' for 'struck'.
Challenge with question, boast, ablative kʷosmōd 'from anyone', neuter plural predicate polh₁úh₂. stn̥h₂ént 'placed/stood' a stretched sense. The last clause's ḱós for the challenger is clear enough.

(1) stesth₂wé is PRF.1DU 'we two stand' for narrative 'Two stood there'; 3du/3pl needed (stesth₂ḗr as in 2d88a4f3). (2) 'Then swear the oath by Sky' uses IMP.3SG dʰéh₁tu; 2sg needed. (3) 'Sky heard, and he died': mért has no subject change, so the PIE says Sky died; h₁énos needed.
'I leave you my spears' drops the dative 'you' (usméy). Otherwise good: VOC pl + 2pl imperatives h₁sté, mē Hrumpté, memn̥té.

'Put down your spear' dʰéh₁tu and 'Take my horses' sléh₂gʷtu are IMP.3SG in a 2sg address (téwe, túH); 2sg needed. Minor: mē + 1sg subjunctive for 'I will not kill you'; h₁opéyetām 'made reach' for 'gave' is stretched.

'Come with your spear' (téwe) uses IMP.3SG gʷémtu; gʷm̥dʰí needed. Minor: gʰóstis 'guest' for 'enemy' (Lat. hostis sense) stretched; h₁ésyo for 'his own'; 'on the field' not rendered in the last scene.
